line: Jung's statements on the child: the child god, the futurity of the motif, and the child as a picture of the preconscious psyche.

sections.title: The child motif
sections.line: CW9i ¶259–271: the child god, and what the motif represents.

quotes.quote: This archetype of the "child god" is extremely widespread and intimately bound up with all the other mythological aspects of the child motif.
In folklore the child motif appears in the guise of the dwarf or the elf as personifications of the hidden forces of nature.
I mention this instance only to demonstrate the enduring vitality of the child archetype.

sections.title: Futurity
sections.line: CW9i ¶278–279: the child motif as an anticipation of what is to come, and its forms of wholeness.

quotes.quote: Hence the occurrence of the child motif in the psychology of the individual signifies as a rule an anticipation of future developments, even though at first sight it may seem like a retrospective configuration.
One of the essential features of the child motif is its futurity.
